paragraphs: Mentioned in Yalkut Shimoni, Emor, remez 642 [supplied רמו תרמ״כ], reporting in R’ Abbahu’s name. Hyman says this was also the reading available to the author of Yuchasin.
But Hyman identifies the source as Vayikra Rabbah, Emor [supplied בכ״ר; compare 27], where the reading is Rabbi Yaakov bar Zevadi.

notes.text: The printed תרמ״כ and כ״ר remain unresolved. The source prints רמו in the reference formula, read contextually as remez, “section.” Akiva and Yaakov are the competing name readings.

The saved whole ToratEmet VayikraRabbah27 scalar explicitly has Rabbi Yaakov bar Zavdi, a matching Emor passage beside supplied בכ״ר. It does not prove a printed letter repair or identify Akiva with Yaakov. The supplied Yalkut locator רמו תרמ״כ remains literal, not silently reordered into a guessed section number. Yalkut and Yuchasin were not newly inspected; Akiva and Abbahu keep abbreviated R'. Hyman’s claimed source priority remains attributed.

The photographed edition gives Yalkut remez 642 (תרמ״ב) and במ״ר אמור. Yalkut Shimoni 642 names Akiva bar Zavdi in Rabbi Abbahu’s name, while the parallel in Vayikra Rabbah 27 names Yaakov bar Zavdi. The consulted Yuchasin OCR lists the bare name Akiva bar Zavdi. Hyman’s report about the reading available to the author of Yuchasin and his identification of the earlier source remain his own. These readings leave the relationship between the two names open.
